subject: AWS Marketplace metering & fulfillment: seller onboarding and usage-claim protocol
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Hart <sophie.hart@clearsight.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace metering & fulfillment: seller onboarding and usage-claim protocol

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, we want to align on the minimal integration surface to onboard ClearSight as an AWS Marketplace SaaS Seller while preserving your existing seat/license model. Key asks from our side to help scope work: 

- Confirm the SKU model you want visible in the Marketplace (consumption SKU vs. seat SKU).
- Clarify entitlement token flow: will you rely on AWS entitlement calls or pass a downstream JWT from your platform?
- Expected event granularity (per-request / per-minute / monthly aggregate).
- Any procurement constraints from your billing team (invoicing cadence, net terms, PO requirements).

Can you loop in the Marketplace Ops contact (if separate) and share any internal requirements doc? We can provision a temporary sandbox listing and a webhook receiver for testing.

I cc'ed Kimberly (PM, fulfillment) and Aditya (integration engineer) — Kimberly, Aditya: can you sketch an initial approach and timeline for a conservative two-week technical integration (metering events + entitlement verification + fulfillment confirmation)?

Thanks —

Laura Bennett
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: none
From: Sophie Hart <sophie.hart@clearsight.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marketplace Ops <marketplace.ops@clearsight.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering & fulfillment: seller onboarding and usage-claim protocol

Laura —

Appreciate the clear list. I've attached our requirements spreadsheet (ClearSight_Marketplace_Requirements.xlsx) which contains how our billing currently maps (seat tiers, overage rules, and a per-session consumption metric we expose for analytics). High level answers: 

- Primary preference: seat-based entitlements surfaced in Marketplace for customer-facing invoices; allow an optional consumption SKU for analytics addons.
- Entitlement flow: Marketplace entitlement check today is used for activation; however, our backend also issues a short-lived access token. We'll need to agree on a canonical activation path (AWS entitlement lookup vs. ClearSight token exchange).
- Event granularity: prefer per-session events consolidated into hourly aggregates for cost efficiency.
- Procurement: most enterprise customers require PO + 30 net; invoices must include marketplace listing id.

Questions from Marketplace Ops: do you support idempotent usage events (we have retries) and can you provide an example webhook schema? Also curious what the rollback story is if a fulfillment confirmation fails mid-provision.

Thanks —

Sophie Hart
Head of Partnerships, ClearSight Analytics
Sophie.Hart@clearsight.com
Attachment: ClearSight_Marketplace_Requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Hart <sophie.hart@clearsight.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering & fulfillment: seller onboarding and usage-claim protocol

Sophie / team —

Thanks for the requirements doc, that's helpful. I've sketched a conservative integration approach below (we'll keep QA-focused milestones and a fallback plan):

1) Entitlement model
- We'll publish two SKUs in Marketplace: a primary seat SKU (visible on invoices) and an optional consumption SKU (for analytics add-ons).
- For activation, Redwood can accept either AWS entitlement checks (we'll validate via AWS APIs) OR a ClearSight-signed activation token. If you want both, we'll prefer AWS entitlement as canonical and fall back to your token when entitlement lookup times out.

2) Metering events and idempotency
- Recommended event: emit per-session usage with a server-side UUID event_id; Redwood will accept idempotent events (event_id param).
- On ingestion we will bucket into hourly aggregates (to reduce per-token processing) and forward aggregate usage to the Marketplace metering API once/hour.

3) Fulfillment confirmation and rollback
- Fulfillment confirmation flows: after entitlement passes, Redwood sends a fulfillment confirmation to Marketplace and calls your provisioning webhook. If provisioning fails within our orchestration, we will mark the fulfillment as failed in our logs and send an automated rollback to your provisioning endpoint (idempotent) plus a Marketplace cancellation call if the entitlement was transient.

4) Test plan and timeline (conservative)
- Day 0–2: Sandbox listing + webhook endpoint exchange; verify entitlement lookup and token exchange (smoke).
- Day 3–7: Ingestion + idempotency tests, simulate retries and network failures.
- Day 8–12: End-to-end fulfillment tests with a small set of pilot customers.
- Day 13–14: Cutover window and production listing.

Aditya: can you confirm the webhook schema we plan to publish? I'm attaching a draft mapping file for your review (metering-mapping-draft.yaml).

Sophie: noting procurement note — we'll make sure invoices include the marketplace listing id and support PO fields in the invoice metadata.

-Kim

Kimberly Park
Product Manager, Fulfillment & Marketplace Integrations
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: metering-mapping-draft.yaml (text, 6KB)

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering & fulfillment: seller onboarding and usage-claim protocol

Team —

This looks good and captures the conservative approach we discussed. Two action items before we proceed to legal and procurement: 

- Jonas, can legal review the proposed fallback (AWS entitlement canonical, token fallback) and confirm any contract wording we need in the SaaS contract / amendment redline? I've attached a placeholder redline for initial comments (amendment-redline.pdf).
- Aditya / Kim, please prepare the sandbox manifest and a sample payload (id, event_id, timestamp, units) we can run through ClearSight's staging environment. If both pass, we'll schedule the pilot cutover for Jul 14–16.

Sophie — thanks for the procurement notes. We'll include PO fields on our invoices and surface listing ids. If you can confirm a small pilot customer list (two accounts) and a staging endpoint, we'll aim for the July pilot.

Laura

Laura Bennett
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
